title: Meeting Rooms
summary: Decide whether one person can attend every meeting in a list without two of them overlapping.

tests.explain: In start order the meetings are [9, 10], [10, 12], [13, 15]. Each one ends no later than the next one starts, and ending at 10 while the next starts at 10 is fine.
The meeting [1, 5] is still running when [4, 6] starts at 4.
With no meetings there is nothing to clash.

hints: Comparing every pair of meetings works but is O(n²). What order would let you compare each meeting with just one other?
Sort the meetings by start time. If any two meetings clash, then some meeting clashes with the one right after it.
After sorting, return false as soon as intervals[i][0] < intervals[i - 1][1]. A meeting that starts exactly when the previous one ends is fine.

complexity.time: O(n log n): the sort dominates the single pass
complexity.space: O(1) extra besides the sort (O(log n) to O(n) depending on the engine)
